summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with dizziness and shortness of breath due to acute on chronic systolic heart failure and severe anemia. His heart failure was exacerbated by fluid overload, likely from increased water intake, and was managed with increased furosemide and a reduction in lisinopril due to borderline hypotension. His anemia, with a hemoglobin of 6.5 g/dL, showed signs of hemolysis, including low haptoglobin and elevated indirect bilirubin, possibly due to mechanical red cell damage from his aortic valve prosthesis. He received three units of packed red blood cells, with partial response, and was started on iron and omeprazole. His INR was supratherapeutic, prompting temporary hold and subsequent restart of warfarin at a reduced dose with close monitoring. He stabilized, with improved symptoms and resolution of lower extremity edema, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in primary care, heart failure, and hematology clinics.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Heart valve replaced by other means
